claims.evidence: After over three decades of iconic RPGs, developer BioWare is closing down and its in-development Mass Effect game is no more. The move comes just months after corporate owner EA was bought out by a group of investment firms for $55 billion. Read more

claims.evidence: EA has closed its longtime studio partner BioWare , the iconic development house behind Mass Effect and Dragon Age, impacting around 50 staff who were in pre-production on the next Mass Effect game. claims.claim: BioWare announced on social media that it is closing and that early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer quotes BioWare's social media statement saying the studio is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending.
claims.quote: Now, after more than three decades of shared adventures, BioWare is closing and early development on the next Mass Effect project is ending.

claims.claim: BioWare's statement listed Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, Mass Effect and Anthem among its games.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer says the statement listed its greatest hits: Baldur's Gate, Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, Mass Effect and Anthem.

claims.claim: The closure came months after EA was bought for $55 billion by Silver Lake, Affinity Partners and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer says the move comes months after EA was bought out for $55 billion by Silver Lake, Affinity Partners (led by Jared Kushner) and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund.

claims.claim: Bloomberg reported that EA plans to cut roughly 400 jobs, about 3 percent of its workforce.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer cites a Bloomberg report that EA is planning to cut roughly 400 jobs across the company, around 3 percent of its total workforce.

claims.claim: A letter to EA staff seen by Bloomberg said the company was making deliberate choices about where to put talent and investment.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer quotes the letter to staff from CEO David Tinson and CSO Cam Weber, as seen by Bloomberg.
claims.quote: Across our portfolio, we're making deliberate choices to align talent and investments where we see the greatest opportunities for players and long-term growth

claims.claim: Dragon Age: The Veilguard failed to meet EA's internal sales expectations, which led to an earlier round of layoffs at BioWare.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer says BioWare's most recent game, Dragon Age: The Veilguard, failed to meet EA's internal sales expectations, leading to another round of layoffs.

claims.claim: IGN dates the shutdown of BioWare to 21 October 2026 and says EA confirmed the next Mass Effect was cancelled.
claims.evidence: IGN says the remaining developers were laid off when the studio was shut down on October 21, 2026, and that EA confirmed Mass Effect 5 was canceled.

claims.claim: An internal trailer for the cancelled game, Mass Effect Universe, appeared online after the closure; it was made for EA leadership, not the public.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer says the internal trailer appeared online, was intended for internal use and was created for EA leadership rather than the public.
claims.quote: The following is in-engine footage from our small team. It uses our pre-production assets.

claims.claim: IGN verified the trailer and Bloomberg's Jason Schreier corroborated its authenticity, after early suspicion that it was AI-generated.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer says there was initial scepticism that it might be AI generated, that IGN quickly verified it and that Jason Schreier corroborated it on Bluesky.

claims.claim: The trailer shows a new protagonist with their own ship and crew, including a Krogan, and a late appearance by Liara from the original trilogy.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer describes a new protagonist navigating the galaxy in their own ship with a crew including a Krogan, fights with guns and biotics, and Liara appearing near the end.

claims.claim: About 50 developers were working on Mass Effect Universe, and EA's cuts also hit Respawn, Maxis, Full Circle and EA Motive.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer says the 50 developers on Mass Effect Universe lost their jobs in EA layoffs affecting 400 employees, which also hit Respawn, Maxis, Full Circle and EA Motive.

claims.claim: YouTuber Dantics, who says he sat on BioWare's Mass Effect player council, claims the game was set more than 600 years after the trilogy, in a galactic Cold War between three factions.
claims.evidence: GamesRadar+ reports Dantics' claims: set more than 600 years after the original trilogy, three major factions in a Cold War, with a mysterious threat in the background.

claims.claim: Dantics also claims players would have been an N7 agent in handcrafted linear missions with freedom in how to complete them.
claims.evidence: GamesRadar+ reports the claim of an N7 agent described as a cross between John Wick and James Bond, and linear handcrafted missions with Hitman-style freedom.
claims.quote: with Hitman-style freedom in how you complete them.

claims.claim: IGN has backed up some of Dantics' comments, citing an anonymous development source.
claims.evidence: GamesRadar+ says IGN backed up some of his comments and reports, citing an anonymous development source, that every major alien race was working in an in-production build.

claims.claim: Dantics says the game was further along than BioWare's statement suggested.
claims.evidence: GamesRadar+ quotes Dantics saying the team was a lot further in development than the statement suggested.
claims.quote: they were a lot further in development than their statement suggested.

claims.claim: Locked Mass Effect cosmetics that had appeared in Battlefield 6's menus with Season Five were removed after the closure.
claims.evidence: Eurogamer says Mass Effect items added to Battlefield 6's cosmetic menus with Season Five, still unavailable to unlock, appear to have been removed after BioWare's closure.

claims.claim: Fans had expected the Battlefield 6 items to mark N7 Day on 7 November.
claims.evidence: IGN says fans suspected the content was coming soon with N7 Day around the corner and notes N7 Day festivities usually come on November 7.

claims.claim: Amazon Prime Video told IGN its Mass Effect TV series is still in the works.
claims.evidence: IGN says Amazon's Prime Video confirmed to IGN that its Mass Effect TV series was still in the works following BioWare's closure.

claims.claim: A change.org petition to save Mass Effect passed 180,000 verified signatures by 25 October.
claims.evidence: PC Gamer, on 25 October, says the #SaveMassEffect petition has passed 180,000 verified signatures.

claims.claim: The petition asks EA to keep developing Mass Effect or license the series to another studio, not to reverse the closure.
claims.evidence: PC Gamer says the petition does not call for EA to walk back the closure but asks for continued development or licensing.
claims.quote: Alternatively, EA could consider licensing the Mass Effect intellectual property to another studio that shares the passion and vision to keep it alive and allow it to flourish anew.

claims.claim: Two days after the closure, IGN put the petition at more than 50,000 signatures.
claims.evidence: IGN on 23 October says fans launched a petition that amassed more than 50,000 signatures.

conflicts.description: BioWare's statement describes the next Mass Effect as in early development; Dantics, per GamesRadar+, claims it was a lot further along. Unresolved.
